- When sentiment turns negative (especially -1.00) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price momentum; avoid over-optimism.
- If model forecast shows a sharp spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, cap the spike to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome consistently underperforms model (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days), apply mean reversion bias: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend + negative sentiment, expect a 2–3 day lag in true price drop — adjust forecast to reflect delayed correction.
- If sentiment is uniformly positive (all 1.00) but model overestimates, apply a 1–3% downward bias to prevent overshoot.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope and introduce a 2–3 day “cooling-off” period before re-estimating.
